title: Differentiation of iPSC into Microglia-Like Cells (iMGL) V.2
markdown:
## Protocol: I need to obtain microglia-like cells from human iPSCs for an in vitro cell-culture study. Describe a workflow starting with iPSC maintenance, proceeding through hematopoietic induction and progenitor isolation, and ending with microglial differentiation. Include the culture transitions, cell-handling steps and collection points needed to follow this route.

### Overview

This protocol describes: I need to obtain microglia-like cells from human iPSCs for an in vitro cell-culture study. Describe a workflow starting with iPSC maintenance, proceeding through hematopoietic induction and progenitor isolation, and ending with microglial differentiation. Include the culture transitions, cell-handling steps and collection points needed to follow this route..

### Materials/Reagents

Refer to the source-grounded procedure steps for required reagents.

### Equipment

Refer to the source-grounded procedure steps for required equipment.

### Safety & Sterility

Follow the source-supported safety requirements and institutional procedures.

## Reagent Preparation

### Pre-culture

1. iMGL Diff Base Medium can be kept in storage at 4°C for approximately one month. It is important to make fresh iMGL Diff Complete Medium (addition of fresh cytokines to the base medium) every time you need to feed the culture [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S01 -->
2. iMGL Maturation Media Recipe: iMGL Complete Medium CD200 (100 ng/ml) 100 ug/ml Nov C311 1:10 dilution Cx3CL1 (100 ng/ml) 100 ug/ml Pepro 300-31 1:10 dilution [1] <!-- protocol-step:B01-T0-S02 -->

## Aggregate Plating

### 01:00:00

> **Operational constraint:** Once iPSCs are 70-80% confluent in 2-3 wells of a 6-well tissue culture plate, passage
 and plate the iPSCs as aggregates [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S01 -->
1. Coat a 6-well tissue culture plate with Matrigel for a least 01:00:00 prior to

 passaging cells [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S02 -->
2. ## 4 Set the following media out to warm to Room temperature :

 Dispase
 DMEM/F12
 PBS
 mTesR1 [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S03 -->
3. After plate has been coated for 01:00:00 and media has warmed to

 Room temperature , proceed to passage aggregates as described below: [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T0-S04 -->

### Aggregate Dissociation

1. 5.1 Aspirate media from well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S01 -->
2. 5.2 Wash cells with 2 mL of PBS per well [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S02 -->
3. 5.3 Aspirate PBS from well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S03 -->
4. 5.4 Add Dispase to cells 1 mL per well . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S04 -->
5. 5.5 Incubate at 37 °C for between 00:07:00 and 00:08:00 . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S05 -->
6. 5.6 Aspirate the Dispase from the wells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S06 -->
7. ## 5.7 Gently wash cells 2-3 times with 2 mL of DMEM/F12 per well, aspirating after each

 wash. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S07 -->
8. 5.8 Add 2 mL of DMEM/F12 to each well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S08 -->
9. ## 5.9 Using the StemProEZPassage Disposable Stem Cell Passaging Tool, cut the iPSCs into
 aggregates that are approximately 100-200µm in diameter. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S09 -->
10. 5.10 Transfer the detached aggregates with a serological pipette into a 15 ml conical tube.

 Note

 Check tissue culture plate under microscope to ensure that the majority of
 aggregates have been transferred from the plate.

 Note

 If aggregates still remain, wash well with 2mL of DMEM/F12 and transfer to 15mL
 conical tube [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S10 -->
11. 5.11 Centrifuge 15 ml conical tubes containing cell aggregates at 750 rpm for 00:03:00 . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S11 -->
12. 5.12 Aspirate supernatant from cell pellet. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S12 -->
13. 5.13 Resuspend pellet gently in 2 mL of mTesR1

 Note

 Obtaining a uniform suspension of aggregates approximately 100-200µm in
 diameter is optimal. The StemPro EZPassage Disposable Stem Cell Passaging Tool
 should be used to ensure these aggregate sizes.

 Note

 It is essential that pellet is resuspended by pipetting only one time, this ensures a
 larger degree of cell survival - as cells are incredibly delicate at this stage. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T1-S13 -->

### Aggregate Counting and Calculation

1. 6.1 Pipette 40 µL pf DMEM/F12 into three individual wells of a 96-well flat bottom tissue

 culture plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T2-S02 -->
2. 6.2 Pipette 5 µL of aggregate suspension to each well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T2-S03 -->

### After 24 hours

1. 8 After calculating the number of aggregates to plate per well, aspirate Matrigel from
 previously coated 6-well plate(s) (refer to Step 2), and add 2 mL of mTesR1

 containing 2.5µM Rock Inhibitor to each well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S01 -->
2. 8.1 Gently mix the cell aggregate mixture by inverting 15mL conical tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S02 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Do not vortex or pipette mixture. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S03 -->
3. 8.2 Add the previously calculated volume of aggregate suspension to each well in the 6-well
 plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S04 -->
4. 8.3 Place the plate containing mTesR1 and aggregate suspension in incubator at 37 °C

 for 24:00:00 . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S05 -->
5. Prior to placing plate in incubator, perform a “t” shaped motion with the plate to
 ensure that aggregates are distributed evenly throughout the wells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S06 -->
6. 8.4 After 24 hours, carefully aspirate mTesR1 containing 2.5µM Rock Inhibitor from each
 well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S07 -->
7. 8.5 Gently wash cells with 2 mL of PBS per well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S08 -->
8. 8.6 Aspirate PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S09 -->
9. 8.7 Add 2 µL of pre-warmed fresh mTesR1 to each well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S10 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note

 Aim for at least 20 adhered aggregates per well of a 6-well tissue culture plate

 protocols.io | https://dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bkrvkv66 September 3, 2020 18/28

 Note

 Do not proceed further if < 20 aggregates or > 40 aggregates have adhered to 6-
 well tissue culture plate as differentiation will be compromised [1] <!-- protocol-step:B04-T3-S12 -->

## FACS Sorting and Harvesting

### Harvesting

1. 12.2 Begin harvesting floating cells using a serological pipette or 1mL micropipette, vigorously
 pipette media and cells up and down approximately 2-3 times in the well to break up
 floating cell aggregates. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S01 -->
2. 12.3 Transfer floating cells and media to appropriately sized conical tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S02 -->
3. 12.4 Wash well with 1 mL of DMEM/F12 and transfer to same collection tube, this will

 ensure the majority of floating cells have been collected. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S03 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note

 Be sure that collected cells are kept on ice to avoid cell death. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S04 -->
4. 12.5 Centrifuge the collection tube at 300 x g for 00:05:00 at 4 °C . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S05 -->
5. 12.6 Aspirate supernatant. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S06 -->
6. 12.7 Re-suspend pellet in 5 mL of sterile FACS Buffer (PBS and 2% FBS) . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S07 -->
7. 12.8 Filter the suspension through a 40µm filter into collection tubes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S08 -->
8. 12.9 Centrifuge the collection tube at 300 x g for 00:05:00 at 4 °C . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S09 -->
9. 12.10 Aspirate supernatant. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S10 -->
10. 12.11 Re-suspend pellet in 5 mL of sterile FACS Buffer (PBS and 2% FBS) . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S11 -->
11. 12.12 Begin harvesting Adherent Cells by first adding 1 mL of Accutase to each well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S12 -->
12. 12.13 Incubate at 37 °C for 00:15:00 . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S13 -->
13. 12.14 Add 2 mL of DMEM/F12 to each well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S14 -->
14. 12.15 Triturate vigorously to achieve a single cell suspension. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S15 -->
15. 12.16 Transfer cell suspension to appropriately sized collection tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S16 -->
16. 12.17 Centrifuge the collection tube at 300 x g for 00:05:00 at 4 °C . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S17 -->
17. 12.18 Aspirate supernatant. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S18 -->
18. 12.19 Re-suspend pellet in 5 mL of sterile FACS Buffer (PBS and 2% FBS) . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S19 -->
19. 12.20 Filter the suspension through a 40µm filter into collection tubes. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S20 -->
20. 12.21 Centrifuge the collection tube at 300 x g for 00:05:00 at 4 °C . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S21 -->
21. 12.22 Re-suspend pellet in 5 mL of sterile FACS Buffer (PBS and 2% FBS) . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T0-S22 -->

### Staining

1. 13 To stain cells for FACS sorting, add the following antibodies to the filtered cell
 suspension (cells and FACS Buffer) in the noted concentrations:
 CD34-FITC (1:200)
 CD43-APC (1:200)

 protocols.io | https://dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bkrvkv66 September 3, 2020 22/28

 CD45 - Alexa Fluor700 (1:200) (optional)
 CD41-PE (1:200) (optional) [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T1-S01 -->
2. 14 Incubate cells and antibodies On ice in the dark for 00:20:00 . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T1-S02 -->
3. 15 After incubation, add 2 mL of FACS Buffer to each tube and centrifuge at 300 x g

 for 00:05:00 . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T1-S03 -->
4. 16 Aspirate supernatant. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T1-S04 -->
5. 17 Re-suspend pellet in 500 µL of FACS Buffer . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T1-S05 -->
6. 18 Sort the CD34+ and CD43+cell population using a Becton Dickinson FACSAria II. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T1-S06 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note

 Sorting has to be performed in sterile conditions. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T1-S07 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note

 In order to obtain high quality HPCs, it is suggested to sort only the CD34+ and
 CD43+ double positive cell population, discarding the single or double negative
 cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T1-S08 -->

### Freezing Sorted Cells

1. 19 Centrifuge positively sorted cells at 300 x g for 00:05:00 at 4 °C . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T2-S01 -->
2. 20 Aspirate supernatant. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T2-S02 -->
3. 21 Re-suspend cells at a concentration of 1 million cells per 1 mL of Cryostor CS10 . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T2-S03 -->
4. 22 Aliquot 1 mL of cell and freezing medium suspension per cryovial. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T2-S04 -->
5. 23 Place cells in -80 °C for approximately 48:00:00 . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T2-S05 -->
6. 24 After 48 hours, cells can be transferred to liquid nitrogen for long-term storage. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B06-T2-S06 -->

## Hematopoietic Induction

### Day 0

1. 11.1 Day 0 - Aspirate medium from wells and add 2 mL of Medium A per well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T0-S01 -->

### Day 2

1. 11.2 Day 2 - Gently remove 1 mL of Medium A from each well and gently replace with

 1 mL of fresh Medium A per well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T1-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note

 It is best to use a serological pipette or a 1mL micropipette to perform the media
 removal. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T1-S02 -->

### Day 3

1. 11.3 Day 3 - Aspirate Medium A from wells and gently add 2 mL of Medium B per well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T2-S01 -->

### Day 5

1. 11.4 Day 5 - Gently remove 1 mL of Medium B from each well and gently replace with

 1 mL of fresh Medium B

 per well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T3-S01 -->

### Day 7

1. 11.5 Day 7 - Gently remove 1 mL of Medium B from each well and gently replace with

 1 mL of fresh Medium B

 per well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T4-S01 -->

### Day 10

1. 11.6 Day 10 - Gently remove 1 mL of Medium B from each well and gently replace with

 1 mL of fresh Medium B

 per well. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T5-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note

 As the number of floating cells in the culture increases, it is imperative that media
 changes are done slowly and gently to avoid removing a large number of the floating
 cells. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T5-S02 -->

### twelfth day of
 culture

1. 12.1 Floating and adherent cells should be harvested for FACS sorting on the twelfth day of
 culture for presence of the following cellular markers:
 1) CD43
 2) CD34
 3) CD45 [1] <!-- protocol-step:B05-T6-S01 -->

## iMGL Derivation and Differentiation

### Thawing Sorted Cells

1. 25 Using previously sorted cryopreserved cells (Freezing Down Sorted Hematopoietic
 Stem Cells Section), place frozen vial of cells in 37 °C water bath for quick thaw. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S01 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note

 Thaw should take less than one minute, remove cells from water bath prior to
 complete thaw. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S02 -->
2. 26 Transfer contents of cryovial to a conical tube containing
 8 mL of DMEM/F12 supplemented with 2% FBS . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S03 -->
3. 27 Centrifuge concial tube at 300 x g for 00:05:00 . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S04 -->
4. 28 Aspirate supernatant. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S05 -->
5. 29 Re-suspend cell pellet in iMGL Diff Complete Medium at a concentration of ~500,000
 cells per 2 mL . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S06 -->
> **Operational constraint:** Note

 iMGL Diff Base Medium can be kept in storage at 4°C for approximately one month.
 It is important to make fresh iMGL Diff Complete Medium (addition of fresh
 cytokines to the base medium) every time you need to feed the culture [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T0-S07 -->

### Day 2

1. 30 Day 2 - Add 1 mL of IMGL Diff Complete Medium per well of a 6-well tissue culture

 plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T1-S01 -->

### Day 4

1. 31 Day 4 - Add 1 mL of IMGL Diff Complete Medium per well of a 6-well tissue culture

 plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T2-S01 -->

### Day 6

1. 32 Day 6 - Add 1 mL of IMGL Diff Complete Medium per well of a 6-well tissue culture

 plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T3-S01 -->

### Day 8

1. 33 Day 8 - Add 1 mL of IMGL Diff Complete Medium per well of a 6-well tissue culture

 plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B07-T4-S01 -->

## iPSC Thawing and Initial Culture

### Initial Setup

1. 1.1 To resuspend, thaw aliquot On ice . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S01 -->
2. 1.2 Add 12.5 mL cold DMEM/F12. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S02 -->
3. 1.3 Pipette up and down twice. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S03 -->
4. 1.4 Add 1 mL of Matrigel per well of 6 well plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S04 -->
5. 1.5 Store diluted Matrigel at 4 °C . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S05 -->
6. 1.6 Prior to thawing cells, coat plate with Matrigel for 01:00:00 . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S06 -->
7. 1.7 Add 9 mL DMEM/F12 to a 15 ml conical tube labeled with the iPSC line name and

 passage number. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S07 -->
8. 1.8 Remove cells from liquid nitrogen storage. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S08 -->
9. 1.9 Quickly thaw cells in 37 °C water bath and/or in hands. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S09 -->
10. 1.10 Just prior to complete thaw, remove vial from water bath. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S10 -->
11. 1.11 Transfer the contents of the cryo-vial (~ 1 mL ) into the 15 ml conical tube. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S11 -->
12. 1.12 Spin at 750 rpm for 00:03:00 at Room temperature . [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S12 -->
13. 1.13 Aspirate media. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S13 -->
14. 1.14 Resuspend cells in 2 mL mTesR1 (supplemented with 5 micromolar (µM) —

 10 micromolar (µM) Rock Inhibitor) by pipetting two times. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S14 -->
15. 1.15 Transfer the cell solution to one well of a 6-well plate. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S15 -->
16. 1.16 Incubate at 37 °C Overnight in 6 % CO2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S16 -->
17. 1.17 Replace the media daily until cells are ready to split or analyze. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T0-S17 -->

### Maintenance Phase

> **Operational constraint:** Note

 Media should be changed daily. It is okay to skip a media change one time each
 week if double feeding is performed; however, this is largely dependent on the
 density of the cells and volume of media (do not double feed if cells are more than
 70% confluent). [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S01 -->
1. Aspirate media. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S02 -->
2. 1.19 Gently add fresh mTesR1 to cells (volume depends on cell density and well size).
 0.5 mL per well to 24 well plate

 2 mL — 4 mL per well to 6 well plate
 5 mL — 10 mL to 10 cm2 plate [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S03 -->
3. 1.20 Incubate at 37 °C in 6 % CO2. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S04 -->
4. Under microscope, remove differentiated cells with p20 or p200 tip (depending on the
 amount of differentiation). Transfer the cells/media to a biohazard bag. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S05 -->
5. 1.22 Gently wash cells with 1x PBS. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S06 -->
6. 1.23 Add fresh mTesR1.
 0.5 mL per well to 24 well plate

 2 mL — 4 mL per well to 6 well plate
 5 mL — 10 mL to 10 cm2 plate [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S07 -->
7. 1.24 Incubate at 37 °C in 6 % CO2 until cells are 60 — 80 % confluent. Change mTesR1
 media daily until
 cells are needed. Repeat cleaning as necessary. [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S08 -->
> **Operational constraint:** 1.25 iPSCs grow on Matrigel. Plates should be coated with Matrigel at least 1 hour prior to
 plating and no
 longer than 24 hours prior to plating cells:
 0.5 mL in 12 well plate

 1 mL in 6 well plate
 4 mL in 10 cm2 plate [1] <!-- protocol-step:B02-T1-S09 -->

## References

- [1] Differentiation of iPSC into Microglia-Like Cells (iMGL) V.2 — https://doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bkrvkv66
